summary: django-docutils unsafe Docutils defaults allow local file disclosure, SSRF, and stored XSS
details: ## Summary django-docutils before `0.30.0` rendered reStructuredText through Docutils without protected web-safe defaults. Public rendering paths, including `publish_doctree`, `publish_html_from_source`, `publish_html_from_doctree`, `publish_parts_from_doctree`, the `{% rst %}` template tag, the `rst` template filter, `DocutilsTemplates`, and `DocutilsView`, could process attacker-controlled RST with Docutils directives that read local files, fetch URL-backed content, or emit raw HTML. The issue is fixed in `0.30.0` by disabling Docutils file insertion, raw directives, local `docutils.conf` processing, and unsafe URI schemes by default, and by sanitizing doctrees before HTML is emitted. Applications are affected when they render attacker-controlled or lower-trust RST through django-docutils without their own safe Docutils configuration. Applications that only render trusted static RST are not affected unless that content can be influenced by an attacker. ## Impact An attacker who can influence RST rendered by a vulnerable django-docutils integration may be able to read files readable by the Django worker process, trigger server-side requests through URL-backed directives, or inject raw HTML/JavaScript into rendered output. Examples of affected application patterns include comments, wiki pages, blog bodies, profile or biography fields, CMS fields, uploaded RST documents, API-supplied RST, or overridden view content methods that return user-supplied RST. Potential impact includes disclosure of application configuration, environment files, credentials, source files, templates, mounted secrets, and logs readable by the process. UI escaping after rendering is not sufficient for file disclosure because the server-side read occurs before HTML reaches the client. ## Affected versions Affected package: `django-docutils` on PyPI Affected versions: `<= 0.29.0` Patched versions: `>= 0.30.0` ## Technical details Before `0.30.0`, django-docutils handed RST content to Docutils without forcing these web-safe settings: ```python { "file_insertion_enabled": False, "raw_enabled": False, "_disable_config": True, } ``` Docutils treats file insertion and raw content as legitimate features for trusted documents. In a web application that renders lower-trust RST, those defaults can expose server-side data or emit attacker-controlled HTML unless the application disables the features. The vulnerable behavior included: - `.. include:: ` reading local files - `.. include:: ` fetching URL-backed content server-side - `.. csv-table:: :file:` reading local files - `.. csv-table:: :url:` fetching URL-backed content server-side - `.. raw:: html` emitting unescaped HTML - `.. raw:: html :file:` reading and emitting file-backed raw content - local `docutils.conf` configuration re-enabling unsafe behavior ## Proof of concept This minimal harness uses the public `{% rst %}` template tag. On vulnerable versions, the include directive expands server-side and the raw directive emits unescaped HTML. On fixed versions, both directives are disabled under the default configuration. ```python import django from django.conf import settings settings.configure( INSTALLED_APPS=["django_docutils"], TEMPLATES=[{ "BACKEND": "django.template.backends.django.DjangoTemplates", "DIRS": [], "APP_DIRS": False, "OPTIONS": {"libraries": {"dj": "django_docutils.templatetags.django_docutils"}}, }], # DJANGO_DOCUTILS_LIB_RST intentionally unset == default install. ) django.setup() from django.template import engines dj = engines["django"] def render_user_rst(rst: str) -> str: return dj.from_string("{% load dj %}{% rst content %}").render({"content": rst}) print(render_user_rst(".. include:: /etc/passwd\n")) print(render_user_rst(".. raw:: html\n\n x\n")) ``` Expected behavior on vulnerable releases such as `0.28.0` and `0.29.0`: ```text The include directive emits readable file contents. The raw directive emits x as HTML. ``` Expected behavior on fixed releases such as `0.30.0` and later: ```text The include directive is disabled. The raw directive is disabled. ``` ## Remediation Upgrade to django-docutils `0.30.0` or later. For trusted static RST that intentionally depends on unsafe Docutils features, opt in explicitly: ```python DJANGO_DOCUTILS_LIB_RST = { "allow_unsafe_docutils_settings": True, "docutils": { "raw_enabled": True, "file_insertion_enabled": True, "_disable_config": False, }, } ``` Do not enable unsafe Docutils settings for comments, profile text, CMS fields, uploaded files, API request data, or other lower-trust content. Note: `django-docutils==0.30.0` has an undeclared runtime dependency on `typing-extensions`; install it alongside if your environment doesn't already provide it (tracked separately as a packaging fix). ## Related - django-docutils documentation: - django-docutils 0.30.0: - - - django-docutils security topic: - django-docutils changelog: - django-docutils PyPI: - django-docutils source repository: - Docutils security guide: - Docutils configuration reference: - Django security overview: - Related NiceGUI advisory for the same Docutils sink pattern: - Related NiceGUI CVE entry: ## Credit Thanks to the reporters who disclosed and helped characterize this issue.
